rationale: The transport-corrected execution passed all four cases and, for the first time, witnessed the park at the shipped default event capacity, so the event-backpressure account loses its last measurement limitation and cites that single receipt for both scopes.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled mechanism: the actor publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor builds as `async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity)` (handle.rs:295-323; knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that never consumes the event stream still leaves it unread, and `subscribe_events` only hands out clones of that same channel (handle.rs:254-259). A send that cannot fit parks the actor task, which then cannot run op.tick() (election heartbeats, resends, batch flushes), cannot handle incoming messages and cannot answer any Command - including the append_notify Timeout that drain_notifiers would have produced on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222; endpoint documented at handle.rs:114-137). The crate's sibling egress paths avoid this with try_send (drain_outgoing_buf; push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs). Retained support, execution bbff5b4cad8f47129ee5997bb6eee815 (experiment 90492867f1794b14afa6537c6a7b7951-experiment, exit 0, all four selected tests passed, parsing_error_count 0), read in this order: event 0 `default_capacity_parked_cluster` {event_capacity: 1024, nodes_parked: 2, decided_before: 1129, decided_after: 1129, append_notify_timeout_reached: true} - with the runtime's default event capacity left unchanged, two unread nodes reached the bound and the healthy third node's decided index did not move across a write attempt that ended in the documented Timeout; events 4,5,6 in the same run restate the node-local freeze at capacity 64 (`unconsumed_event_bound_reached` {nodes_full: 2, nodes: 3}, `actor_parked` {node: 1, samples_without_reply: 10, permanently_parked: true}, `append_notify_endpoint_withheld` {node: 1, per_call_deadline_ms: 300, actor_timeout_ms: 1500, resolved: false}); event 3 `parked_majority_cluster` {nodes_parked: 2, healthy_node_responsive: true, decided_before: 3, decided_after: 3} repeats the cluster-level stall at capacity 8 under the same corrected transport; events 2,1 are the control with every event stream drained (`control_actors_responsive` {nodes_answering: 3}, `control_append_notify` {origin: 1, succeeded: true, idx: 2}). The comparison therefore holds at every measured bound and at both scopes: with an unconsumed bounded event channel the actor loop parks, the parked node loses every command endpoint including the documented failure, and once enough nodes park the cluster stops deciding; with the same capacities and activity and a draining consumer nothing freezes. Scope of the defect asserted: a node whose client does not consume its event stream stops participating once it has observed event_capacity transitions, for any finite capacity - now measured at 8, 64 and the shipped default 1024. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the trigger is client-side (a live receiver the application does not read) and no snapshot source states a drain obligation, so the finding rests on the handle-method contract plus the sibling paths' non-blocking design; (b) a dropped receiver unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as a live unread receiver is held; (c) how many nodes a given schedule parks is not bounded (case 1 witnesses at least one permanently parked node while only two of three channels were full, the cluster cases witness two of three); (d) an earlier harness revision used one forwarding task per sender, which jammed behind a parked destination's full incoming channel and produced a spurious stall at nodes_parked 1 in run 8f27d10febbd45dbb6b854e8a2af08c6; the retained receipt is from the corrected per-destination transport, which removes that confound.
limitations: The trigger is client-side (a live receiver the application does not read) and no snapshot source states a drain obligation; the defect rests on the Command/append_notify contract plus the sibling paths' non-blocking design.
A dropped receiver unblocks the actor, so the stall is bounded by how long a live, unread receiver is held.
How many nodes a given schedule parks is not bounded: case 1 witnesses at least one permanently parked node (two of three channels full), the cluster cases witness two of three nodes parked.

The superseded harness revision's transport jam is retained as an excluded cause: run 8f27d10febbd45dbb6b854e8a2af08c6 stalled with only one node parked, and the retained receipt uses the corrected per-destination delivery.
